newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico analysts say U.S. won't lift cement duty.
newsitem.headline: Mexico analysts say U.S. won't lift cement duty.

text.p: Mexican cement industry sources and analysts said Thursday they do not share the Mexican government's optimism that Mexico will win an appeal against anti-dumping duties imposed on cement exports to the United States.
"We see it as a political problem. To uphold an appeal like this could have consequences for forthcoming (U.S.) elections," a Mexican cement industry spokesman said.
Cement analysts meanwhile are not expecting the situation to change in the short or medium term.
"I think all analysts have incorporated a conservative outlook into their scenarios," said Carlos Perezalonso, analyst with the brokerage Santander Investment.
The Mexico-U.S. binational panel, which has been meeting under the auspices of the North American Free Trade Agreement, is expected to rule on Friday.
The panel, however, does not have the final word, but issues a recommendation to the U.S. Department of Commerce.
"It is difficult to tell how long any ruling in Mexico's favor would take to come into effect," said Perezalonso.

"Sincerely, I don't see much change in the short term. A lot has been said about this, but little done," said Paul Rodriguez from the brokerage Caspian Securities, adding that few in Wall Street expected any change.
Mexican cement has been subject to a 61.4 percent import duty in the U.S. since 1990.
